execution_overview.overall_summary: Both tasks executed in Python inside Docker after minor code repairs (numeric coercion for openness and syntax fix). Task1: High openness showed higher ASPL, lower CC, and lower Q relative to low openness; t-tests were highly significant. Task2: Using 90% node-wise partial networks, high openness had higher ASPL; Welch t-test significant with large effect size.

deviations.description: Coerced openness totals (o_ffi, o_bfas, o_neo) to numeric with mean-imputation and rewrote script cleanly to fix a syntax error from a bad edit.
deviations.reason: Dataset had o_neo as strings and prior edit caused a duplicate function definition. Needed to compute composite and execute.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Followed the planned Python path; only coercion and syntax fixes were applied for compatibility.

result_raw.result_text: Compared to low openness, the high openness group's networks show higher ASPL (less interconnected), lower clustering, and lower modularity; all differences are statistically significant.

conclusion.conclusion_text: Results indicate higher openness is associated with more dispersed networks (higher ASPL), contrary to a claim that higher openness should relate to more interconnection (lower ASPL).
